paras: Anolis bartschi, also known commonly as the Pinar Del Rio cliff anole, the western cliff anole, and the west Cuban anole, is a species of lizard in the family Dactyloidae. The species is endemic to Cuba.

Anolis bartschi is a medium-sized anole. Adult males have a typical snout-to-vent length of 7.5 cm (3.0 in) and females 6.4 cm (2.5 in). It is one of only two anoles that completely lack a dewlap (both sexes), the other being the Cuban stream anole (A. vermiculatus).
A. bartschi is native to western Cuba (Pinar del Río Province).
The preferred natural habitat of A. bartschi is forest in limestone karst areas.
A. bartschi is oviparous. It is among the relatively few anole species in which females may lay their eggs together, forming a communal nest in cavities in a steep cliff.
The specific name, bartschi, is in honor of zoologist Paul Bartsch, who collected the holotype.
